findings.summary: note_blame table queried without vault_id scoping in readBlameForNote. Vault A's GET /v1/tasks/<id> response could include Vault B's provenance blame data for identically-named notes (e.g., both vaults have Resources/People/Alice.md). Fix: added vault_id column to note_blame, scoped all reads/writes.

Missing rate limiter on /admin/watchdog. Handler calls execFileSync(pm2, jlist) + execFileSync(df) on every request. Adversary with admin token could script tight polling loop → child-process fork storm. Fix: 5 req/min rate limiter, consistent with other admin endpoints.

Raw execFileSync error message echoed in 500 response body, leaking internal filesystem paths (e.g., /root/grove/ecosystem.runtime.config.cjs). Fix: dropped message field from 500 response; error logged server-side only.

clean_surfaces: v2 tasks SQL scoping: all tasks/task_results/skill_configs use getVaultDb(vaultId) per-vault SQLite — isolation is at storage layer, no vault_id column needed
scheduler vault-ID threading: scheduler-bin.ts reads GROVE_VAULT_ID from env, fails loudly if missing; all DB calls routed through getVaultDb
skill executors (daily-vault-review, dup-people-detection): each reads/writes only from vault.vaultPath / getVaultDb(vault.vaultId)
skill config endpoints: v2-skills.ts handlers receive VaultContext from verified URL slug auth — no unscoped queries
timer unref regression: scheduler.ts explicitly does NOT .unref() its timers (commented)
secondary_findings_deferred: getNoteVoicesAndAges in db.ts (called by hybridSearch) queries note_blame without vault scoping — wrong provenance metadata (not content) when path names collide; impact lower than readBlameForNote. Thread vaultId through hybridSearch in a future sweep.
patterns_observed: 4th week running: cross-vault shared-table scoping is the dominant bug class. Per-vault SQLite (project_per_vault_sqlite_split.md) would structurally prevent this — it removes the possibility of unscoped queries by making vault isolation a storage-layer guarantee.

Stale PR rebase rot recurred: PR #179 had no tracking conflicts (it just conflicted with a newer version of the same file); PR #178 was fine post-rebase. Daily rebase-sweep cron on open PRs with auto-merge armed would prevent next instance.

Multi-agent worktree agents produced chained/duplicate PRs (#181/#182) when both agents happened to read the same upstream commits. Future mitigation: spawn agents with explicit base-branch-is-main constraint in the prompt, verify after all agents return.
